title: Maps from quasi-coherent modules on a flat groupoid quotient
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Algebraic spaces and their small etale sites are [def-trf-algebraic-space]; quasi-coherent modules on them are [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], module sheaves are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and all pullbacks below are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$: its test-scheme points form groupoids, naturally in the test scheme, with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$, and composition $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ (first the second arrow, then the first). Let $\mathcal X=[U/R]$ be the fppf stackification of this presheaf of groupoids [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description, def-pc-fppf-site]. Give $\mathcal X$ its big fppf site and structure sheaf [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]; quasi-coherence there means local presentation by small sums of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$. Write $x:U\to\mathcal X$ for the canonical map. Assume $s,t$ are flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-module and $H$ any big-fppf module sheaf. Put $F_U=x^*F|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}}$ and $H_U=x^*H|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}}$, and similarly let $F_R,H_R$ be restriction along the canonically two-isomorphic maps $x\circ s,x\circ t$. Denote their canonical comparison maps by $c_s^F:s^*F_U\to F_R$, $c_t^F:t^*F_U\to F_R$, $c_s^H:s^*H_U\to H_R$, $c_t^H:t^*H_U\to H_R$. Restriction gives an injective map $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}}(F,H)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(F_U,H_U)$$ whose image is exactly the maps $v$ satisfying $$c_s^H\circ s^*v\circ(c_s^F)^{-1}=c_t^H\circ t^*v\circ(c_t^F)^{-1}:F_R\longrightarrow H_R.$$ The comparisons for $F$ are isomorphisms. This bijection onto the indicated subset is natural in $F,H$; no local quasi-coherence or flat comparison property is required of $H$.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P=[U/_{p}R]$. By [lem-sfb-stackification-module-equivalence], precomposition along $q:\mathcal P\to[U/R]$ is an equivalence on all module sheaves, preserves quasi-coherence, and has value $(q^*K)(y)=K(qy)$. Thus it identifies the Hom sets and the restrictions and comparisons in the statement. Work on $\mathcal P$. Its objects are $(T,u)$ with $u:T\to U$. An arrow $(T,u)\to(T',u')$ is $(f,r)$ with $f:T\to T'$, $r:T\to R$, $sr=u$, $tr=u'f$. It factors as the groupoid arrow $(\mathrm{id}_T,r):(T,u)\to(T,u'f)$ followed by the special arrow $(f,eu'f):(T,u'f)\to(T',u')$. This is the definition of arrows and composition in the presheaf groupoid.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), proof; the omitted arrow-compatibility check is expanded in steps 3--4 and the injectivity argument in step 5.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-space-module-comparisons] on $\mathcal P$, and put $M=F_U$. It gives quasi-coherence of $M$, the isomorphisms $c_s^F,c_t^F$, and, for each $(T,u)$, an isomorphism $c_u^F:u^*M\to F_{(T,u)}$. For a proposed compatible $v:M\to H_U$, define $$b_u=c_u^H\circ u^*v\circ(c_u^F)^{-1}:F_{(T,u)}\to H_{(T,u)},\qquad \phi_{(T,u)}=\Gamma(T,b_u).$$ On scheme tests [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] identifies $F(T,u)$ with $\Gamma(T,F_{(T,u)})$; the equality $H(T,u)=\Gamma(T,H_{(T,u)})$ follows directly by evaluating its small-etale restriction at $T\to T$. Thus these are module maps between the actual values of the two sheaves.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), proof; the omitted arrow-compatibility check is expanded in steps 3--4 and the injectivity argument in step 5.

proof.text: For a special arrow over $f:T\to T'$ put $u=u'f$, and let $c_f^K:f^*K_{(T',u')}\to K_{(T,u)}$ be the comparison for $K=F,H$. The composition law in [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-space-module-comparisons] gives $c_u^K=c_f^K f^*c_{u'}^K$. Substitution into the definition of $b_u$, using invertibility only for the $F$ comparisons, gives $$b_u\circ c_f^F=c_f^H\circ f^*b_{u'}.$$ On sections the comparisons are adjoint to restriction, so this is exactly the naturality square for the special arrow. It also covers identity arrows.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), proof; the omitted arrow-compatibility check is expanded in steps 3--4 and the injectivity argument in step 5.

proof.text: For a groupoid arrow $k=(\mathrm{id}_T,r):a=(T,sr)\to b=(T,tr)$ write $k^K:K_b\to K_a$ for restriction; these are isomorphisms because $k$ is invertible. Regard $K_R$ using the source test, and let $d^K:r^*K_R\to K_a$ be its comparison. The composition law of [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-space-module-comparisons], including the specified two-isomorphism between the source and target tests, says $$d^K r^*c_s^K=c_{sr}^K,\qquad d^K r^*c_t^K=k^K c_{tr}^K.$$ Pull back the equality imposed on $v$ along $r$, compose on the left with $d^H$, and on the right with $(d^F)^{-1}$. The first side becomes $b_{sr}$, and the second becomes $k^H b_{tr}(k^F)^{-1}$, by these two identities. Hence $b_{sr}k^F=k^H b_{tr}$. This is naturality for $k$. Together with the factorization in step 1 and the special-arrow square, it proves naturality for every $(f,r)$. The maps $\phi$ therefore form a morphism of big-fppf module sheaves. No comparison for $H$ has been inverted.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), proof; the omitted arrow-compatibility check is expanded in steps 3--4 and the injectivity argument in step 5.

proof.text: For any global morphism $\psi:F\to H$, naturality of comparisons in [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-space-module-comparisons] gives $\psi_R c_s^F=c_s^H s^*\psi_U$ and $\psi_R c_t^F=c_t^H t^*\psi_U$. Inverting the $F$ comparisons proves necessity of the displayed equality for $v=\psi_U$. At every $(T,u)$ the same naturality gives $$\psi_{(T,u)}c_u^F=c_u^H u^*v,\qquad \psi_{(T,u)}=c_u^H u^*v(c_u^F)^{-1}=b_u.$$ Evaluating at $T$ forces every component of $\psi$, so two morphisms with the same restriction to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ are equal. Restriction is therefore injective.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), proof; the omitted arrow-compatibility check is expanded in steps 3--4 and the injectivity argument in step 5.

proof.text: If $u:T\to U$ is etale, all its comparisons are the restriction identifications. Consequently $b_u$ is precisely $v$ on this chart, so the constructed $\phi$ restricts to $v$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. Steps 2--5 prove the claimed image and injectivity, and step 1 transfers them to $[U/R]$. Precomposition by a quasi-coherent source map and postcomposition by any target map commute with restriction. Uniqueness of extension therefore makes the inverse on compatible maps commute with both operations; this proves naturality in $F,H$. The given flatness and local finite presentation hypotheses have been retained, although this construction does not need them.
